title: legal redlines scratchpad - enterprise inference contract
content:
Purpose: notes + fast reference for common redlines we should push back on in enterprise inference contracts. This is a personal scratchpad - not final language.

Top-level negotiation goals:
- Protect platform liability while keeping enterprise customers happy (limit liability to fees, but carve out gross negligence/willful misconduct).
- Preserve Redwood's ability to run and improve models (no retroactive training ban on our pre-existing models; limit customer claims over model outputs).
- Clear data handling: customer input and customer-provided data = customer property; customer outputs = generally licensed back to customer; no training on customer data unless explicit TOS add-on.
- Maintain operational flexibility: maintenance windows, reasonable SLAs, limited audit rights.

Clauses to watch / typical redline responses:
1) Indemnity / liability cap
   - Customer often wants unlimited or very high caps for data breach/model harm.
   - Push: liability cap = greater of (12 months fees OR $XMM). For enterprise deals, can negotiate up to 24 months fees with exec sign-off.
   - Carve-outs: no cap for (i) gross negligence/willful misconduct; (ii) IP infringement where Redwood materially contributed; (iii) data breach due to Redwood breach (but try to keep cap still).
   - Sample counter: "Liability cap shall not exceed the aggregate fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim, except for liability arising from gross negligence or willful misconduct."

2) Data usage / training
   - Watch for clauses that claim a broad right to use customer data to improve models.
   - Push: explicit clause that Redwood will not train models on customer-provided confidential data or PII without separate opt-in addendum. Operational telemetry/metrics aggregated and anonymized is OK.
   - Logging: provide limited runtime logs for debugging; delete on request (with reasonable retention window).
   - Sample counter: "Provider may collect aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry. Provider will not use Customer Content to train or improve Provider models without Customer's prior written consent."

3) IP / output ownership
   - Customers want ownership of outputs; we can grant a license but must preserve model IP.
   - Push: Customer owns the outputs they receive (or granted a perpetual, worldwide license), but Provider retains all rights to the models, improvements, and underlying training data.
   - Watch for assignment language that attempts to transfer model IP or derivative rights.

4) Security / audit rights
   - Customers request broad audit rights. Try to limit to SOC2/ISO reports + on-site/audit only for high-tier deals with NDA and scope limits.
   - KMS/HSM: support for customer-managed keys for Private deployments; hosted customers: offer bring-your-own-key for enterprise plan.

5) SLA / uptime / credits
   - Customers want strict SLOs at enterprise scale (p99 latency, throughput guarantees). We can offer p95/p99 latency targets with credits, but avoid hard refunds that act as revenue-based penalties.
   - Define scheduled maintenance windows, notification periods, and exclusion carve-outs (force majeure, customer-caused issues, beta features).
   - Credits formula should be capped (e.g., max X% monthly invoice).

6) Export controls / compliance
   - Ensure customer obligations for export-controlled inputs; Redwood to comply with applicable export laws.

7) Subprocessors / third parties
   - Hosted: list typical cloud providers and allow replacements with notice. For Private, ensure subproc usage is narrower.

8) Termination / data return + transition assistance
   - On termination, offer export of customer data within 30 days. For private/on-prem, ensure we provide configuration/hand-over docs. Transition assistance can be an optional paid service.

Redline language snippets to propose quickly:
- Data use: "Provider will not use Customer Content to improve or retrain Provider models without Customer's prior written consent. Provider may collect aggregated and anonymized usage metrics for service improvement."
- Liability: "Except for liability arising from gross negligence or willful misconduct, either party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the total fees paid by Customer to Provider under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim."
- SLA: "Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide the Service with an uptime of 99.9% measured monthly. Service credits are Provider's sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet uptime targets."

Open questions / items to check with other teams:
- SRE: what is realistic p95/p99 latency and burst tolerance for Dedicated vs Hosted? Need numbers to push back on strict latency SLAs. (Ticket: SRE-291)
- Product: which model variants can be offered as guaranteed fallbacks for availability? Can we commit to model-level equivalence?
- Applied ML: confirm training-on-customer-data policy for Private deployments.
- Sales: what's our standard commercial concession for top-tier enterprise customers (cap increases, custom indemnity)?

Practical negotiation playbook (short):
- First pass: accept reasonable customer ask on outputs + data ownership, reject training-on-data broad rights, propose 12-month fee cap.
- If customer pushes on liability: escalate to VP Legal + Finance and consider increasing cap to 24 months fees OR set fixed $MM floor only for high-revenue deals.
- For audit requests: offer SOC2 + redacted logs; on-site audits only with strict scope, timing, and cost sharing.

Quick TODOs:
- Draft standard "no-training" clause for Legal templates (Asha) - due 2026-03-05.
- Confirm KMS support matrix with infra (Noah) - ask for doc links.
- Pull recent SLA performance reports for last 6 months to support our uptime claims (SRE-291).
- Add sample language for transition assistance + fees to standard playbook.

Notes to self:
- Keep negotiation tone collaborative; customers want predictability. Be pragmatic on outputs ownership but firm on model IP and training rights.
- Record any customer-specific concessions in Salesforce/opportunity record (LEGAL-78).

References:
- Contract Playbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Contract-Playbook
- Recent enterprise redline summary: LEG-2025-Q4-summary (internal)
- Slack: #legal-contracts thread for ACME deal (slack://channel?team=T12345&id=C56789)

---
End of scratchpad. Keep this as living doc; update after calls with SRE/Product/Applied ML.
